newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FEATURE-Brazil bikini-makers eye Europe's beaches.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE-Brazil bikini-makers eye Europe's beaches.

text.p: Brazil's hot little beach numbers, the world-famous "dental floss" bikinis, are looking to grow -- not in size but in popularity.

The makers of the sexy, colourful bits of material that barely cover the nipple and expose the buttocks are on the march to conquer new beaches when the summer season in the southern hemisphere fades and bikini sales slump.

"Swimwear sells well between August and January, but no one buys between February and August," Mara Futema, owner of the Ponte & Arte bikini factory in Salvador, Bahia, said. "Why not export some of what Brazil is good at?"

Indeed, Brazilians have turned the act of going to the beach into an art form that starts with the bikini, moves on to a matching skirt or hot pants, earrings, bag and hair elastic and ends when the beach goddess spreads her sarong on the sand in the hope of being admired by all.

This requires a great deal of preparatory work involving several hours in the gym to tone those muscles, flatten that stomach and firm that derriere so all can be flaunted under the sun. And if that doesn't work, one of Brazil's legion of plastic surgeons can come to the rescue to tuck or liposuck the unwanted fat cells away.

Futema wants to exploit Brazil's beach expertise and has joined forces with six other bikini makers from Salvador in a consortium to stage a multi-coloured lycra attack on Europe's crowded summer beaches.
Their Bahia Brasil Moda Praia (Bahia Brazil Beach Fashion) label received resounding applause for its bikini designs put on show for potential European buyers early this year.
EVERYONE WANTS A BIT OF NEAR-NOTHING
"We were overwhelmed," Futema said. "Retailers wanted to buy up everything then and there. They loved the bright colours, the patterns, the lycra, and they loved the styles."

The consortium aims to sell its minimalist wares initially in Portugal and Spain where language and culture provide an easy link, but it is looking to move further afield eventually -- to France, Switzerland, Italy, Florida and even as far away as Japan.

Requests from interested buyers have been pouring in even from such unlikely destinations as Morocco. But Futema said they were moving cautiously and studying the new markets closely to get a good understanding of the different tastes and cultures.
"We will have to adapt our bikinis somewhat," she said. "The Brazilian body is quite different from the European. European women tend to have larger breasts and flatter behinds."

Futema said the collection would include a Brazilian model and a model to accomodate the more conservative tastes of mainland Spain, which unlike Portugal and the Canary Islands is not as accepting of the risque Brazilian style.

Bahia Brasil Moda Praia is not the first Brazilian bikini maker to move abroad, but it is the first time beachwear manufacturers have teamed up in a consortium to cut costs and increase capacity to accomodate potentially large orders.
If all goes well, the first Brazilian specimen could be spotted on the beaches of Portugal, where the consortium plans to open its first shop this summer.
